ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification and vetting of politically exposed persons under CMF L561-10; systematic screening of all UBOs and shareholders against UN/EU sanctions lists, the French DG Trésor national financial sanctions list, FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements, and OFAC SDN List as best practice; ongoing monitoring at intervals not exceeding 24 hours for list changes and before any capital movement or issuance of shares.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI Registre National des Entreprises (RNE - Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises); consultable via infogreffe.fr and annuaire-entreprises.data.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be comprehensible in French and inserted in the articles of association in Latin script; any foreign-language element must be transliterated into Latin characters and submitted with a French translation; the name must not be contrary to public order or good morals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon refusal of the desired name, the applicant or its agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the INPI within 15 days from the date of refusal, attaching the preliminary search certificate and explanation of intended use; if the refusal is based on a prior trademark right, the applicant may issue a cease-and-desist letter to the trademark owner or initiate an action before the tribunal judiciaire; if refused due to prohibited sensitive tokens, the company must either remove the token or obtain prior ministerial authorization from the competent ministry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual registered office address is accepted for formation and correspondence purposes in France, but the company must maintain accounting records and statutory documentation at an accessible physical location; for a medical device OEM, the registered office may be virtual only if an operational address is established in France for compliance and regulatory inspection; full virtual-only substance will be treated as non-compliant for licensing and tax residence purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% unannounced on-site inspection probability in the first 18 months after incorporation, given the medical device regulatory environment and French anti-fraud measures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.227-1 to L.227-20, L.123-1 et seq., R.123-1 et seq., and Articles L.225-3 and L.225-14 as applicable to SAS capital subscriptions and contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés maintained by the competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce), with mandatory filing through the INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of incorporation and registration filed through the INPI Guichet unique, accompanied by the signed SAS articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, and supporting documents; the historical M0 form is no longer the primary filing channel.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Cash contributions are deposited into a bank or qualifying deposit account, and the deposit certificate is used for registration. Contributions in kind require valuation by a commissaire aux apports unless the statutory exemption conditions are satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The shareholders, acting as the duly constituted corporate body of the Company, resolve to approve the subscription and payment of the share capital described in the Articles of Association and to issue the corresponding shares. The registered office is adopted at [full French address], with authority to update the registration records accordingly. [Name] is appointed Président for the term and remuneration specified in the Articles. [Name] is appointed Directeur Général, if applicable, with the powers specified in the Articles. The officers are authorized to complete all banking, registry, tax, employment, insurance, and licensing formalities necessary to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Structure and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises; competent commercial court registry for RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the SAS name, registered office, business purpose, share capital, shareholders, Président, and any Directeur Général. Obtain a valid premises title, domiciliation agreement, or registered-office authorization. Verify that the corporate purpose covers design, manufacture, assembly, import, distribution, and servicing of radiology detector equipment.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and business-purpose statement
Registered-office lease, domiciliation contract, or premises occupancy evidence
Officer identification, declarations of non-conviction, and certificates of parentage where required
Power of attorney for filing representative, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the corporate purpose, address, identity data, or supporting evidence and resubmit through the INPI portal. Obtain a written registry query if the legal basis for rejection is unclear.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles and Subscribe Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders, appointed Président, and depositary bank or regulated financial institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles of association and subscription schedule. Pay at least 50% of cash contributions into a blocked capital account. Obtain the certificate of deposit. Document any contribution in kind and obtain a commissaire aux apports report unless a statutory exemption is validly applied.
required_dossiers: Final signed SAS articles of association
Bank account opening and capital-deposit file
Contribution-in-kind valuation report or exemption decision
Shareholder powers of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank or KYC deficiencies, replace incomplete identification documents, and obtain a corrected deposit certificate before filing. Do not file until the subscribed amount matches the articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal-notices publication service in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the statutory incorporation notice in an authorized journal or approved online legal-notices service. Ensure the notice states the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, Président, and registration details required by applicable regulations. Retain the publication certificate.
required_dossiers: Final articles or incorporation data sheet
Identity and appointment details of the Président and other mandatory officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication where mandatory information is omitted or inaccurate. Upload the corrected certificate to the INPI filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Registration and Beneficial Ownership Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, transmitting the file to the competent RCS registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic incorporation formalities, upload the signed articles and supporting evidence, identify the beneficial owners, pay the applicable registration charges, and monitor the portal for registry queries. Ensure the beneficial-owner analysis identifies natural persons ultimately owning or controlling the SAS or, where none can be identified, the legally designated senior managing officer.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder corporate documents, legalized or apostilled and translated where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer the registry query within the stated deadline, upload corrected or legalized documents, and pay any supplemental charge. If refused, request the written grounds and file an amended application or pursue the applicable registry appeal route.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Post-Registration Corporate and Tax Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIE (Service des impôts des entreprises), URSSAF, competent bank, and INPI Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN, SIRET, and Kbis extract; release the capital account; open the operating account; activate VAT and corporate-tax accounts; register as an employer before hiring; establish accounting records and mandatory registers; and adopt the first board or shareholder resolutions required by the articles.
required_dossiers: Accounting engagement and statutory register package
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or social-security account mismatches through the relevant service portal and preserve written confirmation. Do not employ personnel or invoice regulated activities before the relevant registrations and insurance are effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Medical-Device, Industrial, and Site Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM), competent prefecture and DREAL, labour inspectorate, and local fire-safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the detector is a medical device, component, accessory, or non-medical industrial product. For products within Regulation (EU) 2017/745, establish the applicable classification, conformity-assessment route, technical documentation, quality system, post-market surveillance, and CE-marking position. Register the economic operator with ANSM where required. Screen the site against ICPE and water-law rules before construction or operation, and obtain any required declaration, registration, or authorization.
required_dossiers: Product intended-purpose and regulatory classification memorandum
Quality-management-system documentation, normally ISO 13485-based where applicable
Declaration of conformity and notified-body documents, if applicable
ANSM economic-operator registration evidence, if applicable
ICPE screening and prefectural declaration, registration, or authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to ANSM, prefectural, DREAL, or fire-authority observations with revised technical documents, corrective measures, and a formal resubmission. Escalate unresolved administrative decisions through the applicable French administrative appeal process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Ecological Transition through the competent prefecture and DREAL (Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement); ANSM is the competent French authority for applicable medical-device operator and product obligations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No universal manufacturing licence applies solely because the activity is SAS manufacturing. Depending on the process and site, the required instrument is an ICPE declaration, ICPE registration, or ICPE authorization under the nomenclature of classified installations, together with applicable ANSM medical-device obligations and CE conformity assessment under Regulation (EU) 2017/745.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, competent prefecture, and DREAL environmental assessment authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Site- and process-dependent: generally no standalone full EIA for ordinary detector assembly, but an environmental examination and ICPE screening are required; a full environmental assessment applies only where the project meets the relevant regulatory thresholds or case-by-case criteria.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with applicable ICPE ministerial orders, Water Act requirements, prefectural prescriptions, and EU waste rules. Wastewater limits, VOC limits, air-emission controls, hazardous-substance storage, and waste classification are permit- and process-specific. Maintain traceability for hazardous waste through the French Trackdéchets system and use authorized treatment operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before occupation, obtain required fire-safety compliance evidence under the building and workplace rules, including emergency exits, fire detection or suppression systems, electrical conformity, and safe storage of chemicals. Secure structural-load and equipment-installation verification where relevant. Complete the employer's occupational-risk assessment document (DUERP), worker training, machinery conformity checks, and, if ionizing radiation sources or X-ray-generating equipment are operated, radiation-protection arrangements and regulatory declarations or authorizations through the applicable ASN framework.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy and Finance; portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration via Guichet unique (INPI) and Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register with Guichet unique (INPI) to obtain SIREN/SIRET from INSEE; French VAT ID is FR + 2-digit key + SIREN. Non-EU established taxable persons generally require a fiscal representative and bank guarantee. Application to SIE with constitutive documents, proof of address, ID, mandates, Kbis extract, and VAT registration form. Registration required before first taxable transaction; non-resident B2B VAT registration via SIE. Simplified e-commerce regimes may apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; SAS is subject to French corporate income tax at 25% (2025) on worldwide income if French tax resident. Territorial scope: French-source income for non-residents; foreign operations may be exempt under tax treaties. No pass-through default.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box. Available elections: tax transparency option under Art. 239 bis AA CGI (conditions: industrial/commercial activity, limited shareholders); fiscal integration/consolidation under Art. 223 A CGI (95% ownership); parent-subsidiary regime under Art. 145 CGI (5% participation); VAT group/assujetti unique under Art. 256 C CGI; hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD2 and interest limitation under Art. 212 bis CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) / VAT
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis for non-established taxable persons making B2B supplies in France. Domestic franchise en base thresholds: EUR 85,000 (goods) / EUR 37,500 (services) from 2025 (2024: EUR 91,900 / EUR 36,800). EU-wide EUR 10,000 threshold for cross-border B2C distance sales and services. Registration required before first taxable transaction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates B2B e-invoicing via certified PDPs (Plateformes de Dématérialisation Partenaires) with e-reporting to DGFiP. Timeline: September 2026 for large/mid-sized issuers and all receivers; September 2027 for all issuers. Formats: Factur-X, UBL, CII. No real-time clearance like Italy; structured invoice data and lifecycle statuses transmitted to tax authority. Chorus Pro for public sector. Non-resident VAT representatives may require API connectivity; digital stamping not required, but electronic signature/audit trail is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations exempt under Art. 262-I CGI; intra-EU supplies exempt under Art. 262-ter CGI if valid VAT ID and transport proof. Offshore services exempt under Art. 262-II CGI if directly linked to export/intra-EU supply, or under Art. 259-A CGI for B2B services outside France. Zero-rating requires commercial invoice, customs export declaration, transport/proof of exit, and consideration received.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR
Commercial invoice with VAT exemption reference
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT confirmation
Intra-EU: EC Sales List and VAT ID validation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP audits export zero-rating, intra-EU supplies, and VAT refunds. Fraudulent claims trigger retrospective assessment up to 3 years (10 years for hidden activity/aggravated fraud), 40% penalty for intentional breach, 80% for fraudulent intent, 5% late payment interest, and criminal penalties under Art. 1741 CGI (up to 5 years imprisonment and EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated up to 7 years and EUR 3,000,000). Customs false declaration penalties under Code des douanes; joint liability for fiscal representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France fully liberalises current-account and capital-account payments for both EU and non-EU transactions, with no remaining exchange-control licensing, surrender, or quantitative conversion limits. The euro is freely convertible at market rates. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is possible without foreign-exchange authorisation: a French SAS distributes dividends through the paying agent, while the non-resident parent may be exempt from French withholding tax under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (for EU/EEA parents with at least 5% shareholding), or receive treaty relief under the applicable double-tax treaty; otherwise French statutory withholding (captive at 25% or 30% as applicable) is collected. Inward direct investment is subject only to ex-post balance-of-payments reporting and, if the investor is non-EU and the sector is not among the regulated list (defence, dual-use, energy safety etc.), no prior screening is required for ISIC 3250 digital X-ray flat-panel manufacturing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender rule, mandatory conversion ratio, or fixed repatriation deadline applicable to France. Export invoices in foreign currency may be collected in fully retained foreign-currency accounts opened with a French credit institution or may be converted on the interbank market at any time. Banks are nonetheless required to observe the EU Payment Services Regulation and the French Monetary and Financial Code by reporting every individual transaction with non-residents when the amount exceeds EUR 12,500, through the bank's automated balance-of-payments declaration; cash and bearer instruments crossing the French border must be declared to customs from EUR 10,000. Thus, in a practical treasury protocol, export proceeds should be credited to the company's EUR or FX account within the contractual payment date (usually 30–120 days), but the delay is civil and trade-credit driven, not an exchange-control deadline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EUR collections and remote treasury onboarding; Low for large trade-finance commitments. An EEA-licensed electronic-money institution (EMI) or payment institution holding an ACPR passport (e.g., Qonto, Shine, Wise Business, Bunq) may legally maintain a French business payment account and provide an IBAN, SEPA transfers, and MT103 wires through its sponsor bank. However, these platforms generally cannot issue commercial letters of credit, act as negotiating bank, or provide settlement insurance; transfer caps and tier-1 bank sponsor risk may become a treasury bottleneck for an OEM with EUR/USD payables above EUR 100,000 per transaction. Offshore EMIs without an EEA/ACPR licence are not a legal substitute for a French resident SAS account; using such institutions creates a contravention of the Electronic Money Directive and triggers enhanced AML scrutiny by counterparties. Therefore, an ACPR-licensed fintech is an operational complement but not the primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted. French AML/KYC law (Articles R561-5-2 and D561-11 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, as updated by ACPR application guidance) accepts electronic video identification with live biometric verification; physical appearance is not mandatory for a low-risk French SAS. A non-EEA or private-wealth director/beneficial owner would, however, be exchanged by the bank's compliance with a structured remote KYC interview, notarised copies, and source-of-wealth review. The bank may also require a physical visit at its branch or a French notary for signing the mandate if the board resolution is foreign, because French banking law requires legalisation of foreign corporate documents. In all cases the bank needs the original or certified power-of-attorney, board resolution / statuts, UBO register, and the identity documents/proof of address of each signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EU ultimate beneficial owner located in a jurisdiction without a strong tax-cooperation rating, where the ownership chain contains more than three intermediate holding vehicles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) proving ownership; legalised and apostilled corporate documents of each holding tier; six months of personal and corporate bank statements showing source of wealth; passport copies with residential address; a group organisational chart; a management statement explaining the commercial rationale; and French-legal acceptance of the KYC questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The product (digital X-ray flat panel detectors) falls into the category of regulated medical devices, and customers in certain emerging markets may be screened as non-cooperative or health-care payment fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CE certificate and EU Declaration of Conformity under MDR 2017/745; ISO 13485 certificate; executed commercial invoices; customs import/export declarations and EORI number confirmation; manufacturer's product license; end-user certificate stating the final physical location of the detectors; and product liability insurance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bursts of incoming capital from multiple related-party accounts or from shareholders with domicile outside the EEA, creating confusion in the bank's balance-of-payments purpose-code mapping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board minutes authorising the capital increase; intercompany loan agreements or equity subscription documentation; source-of-funds statements for the funds; a defined treasury policy (politique de trésorerie) specifying the purpose and expected settlement date; and an attestation from a French certified accountant (expert-comptable) on the tax and cash treatment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse-media or sanctions screening hits on a director/beneficial owner due to a name similar to a designated person, or a transaction involving a geographic area that appears on the French Trésor's high-risk list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent PEP and sanctions screening report for each director and shareholder; a written explanation letter; passports with personal identifiers; certificate of non-conviction in the director's jurisdiction; and a legal opinion from a French avocat confirming that neither the entity nor the officer is subject to EU, US, or UN sanctions, and that the shipment will not be re-exported to an embargoed country (with the end-user certificate as backup).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol: SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank high-value) transmitted to the French beneficiary account, with the 'purpose of payment' field populated using the appropriate ISO 20022 code — 'EQUI' for equity/share-premium injection, 'LOAN' for shareholder debt or convertible loan, and, if the platform cannot represent the code, the freetext 'Direct investment in France' in field 70. The receiving bank reconciles the flow to Banque de France's balance-of-payments reporting. Verification requires: (i) an executed shareholder/capital-increase resolution; (ii) updated statuts showing the new shareholding; (iii) registration of the UBO in the RBE; (iv) a bank-issued attestation de dépôt for the escrowed funds if this is an incorporation; (v) a French authorised controller's certificate for a capital increase, if applicable. No prior exchange-control authorisation is needed for a French SAS in ISIC 3250, unless the flow hits the direct investment restrictions in strategic sectors (not applicable).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) for EU suppliers via Target2; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for third-country invoices (USD, CNY, GBP) with the seller's IBAN/BIC and the buyer's export customs (EORI) reference; (iii) irrevocable documentary credit (Commercial LC) issued pursuant to UCP600 for component imports of significant value, with the SAS presenting invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, bill of lading/airway bill and quality certificate through the bank; (iv) documentary collection (D/P, D/A) under URC522 for established suppliers; (v) bank payment undertakings/ramp-ups for recurring trade lanes, with settlement through the bank's confirming house. Each outward remittance must carry the matching invoice number and tax (VAT) references; trade loans on French banks may be drawn in EUR or USD to fund large outbound payments, subject to the parent's guarantee or standby LC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla foreign exchange forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) quoted by a French credit institution under ISDA 2002/CSA
Foreign exchange options and barrier options for tactical hedging of USD or CNY purchase payables
Cross-currency swaps and long-term FX swaps for managing multi-year EUR/CNH or EUR/USD funding positions
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies subject to regulatory restrictions (e.g., INR, BRL) where the French bank's offshore branch or a major global dealer is used for settlement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may compel approval; directors may incur liability for failure to comply. No automatic strike-off deadline applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and applicable management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) through the Company Formalities Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval; within two months when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit may result in a civil fine of EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance, court injunctions, and director liability. France has no fixed automatic administrative strike-off period for late accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return and annual tax package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a financial year ending on 31 December, generally by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; electronic filing is mandatory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased surcharges for formal notices or persistent default, late-payment interest, and tax-audit exposure. No corporate strike-off is automatically triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the Company Formalities Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No general annual confirmation is required when information remains unchanged; changes must generally be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing may result in criminal penalties, including a fine of up to EUR 7,500 and imprisonment of up to six months, together with judicial compliance measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business tax compliance, including CFE review and declarations where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE is assessed annually; applicable declarations generally follow tax-administration deadlines, commonly before the relevant 3 May or year-end deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate declarations may cause assessment based on available information, tax surcharges, late-payment interest, and audit exposure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the relevant statutory test date: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, or 50 employees. Additional group-company rules and specific legal circumstances may independently require an auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Plan (Plan comptable général). IFRS applies where legally required or voluntarily permitted, particularly for qualifying consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not impose a general annual UBO confirmation where the filed information remains unchanged. The SAS must monitor ownership, control, management, and UBO data continuously and file an amendment generally within 30 days after a change. Share transfers must be recorded in the securities movement register and individual securities accounts, and reflected in the UBO filing where control or beneficial ownership changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of share movements (registre des mouvements de titres) and individual securities accounts
Register or record of corporate decisions and shareholder resolutions (registre des décisions)
Minutes and supporting records of shareholder and management decisions
No standalone statutory register of directors is generally required for an SAS; president and other legal representatives must be accurately recorded with the Commercial Registry

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-1,800 per year for a standard registered-office and corporate secretarial package; higher for substantial mail handling or regulated support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,500-12,000 per year for a small SAS subject to statutory audit; complex, group, or regulated operations may cost materially more

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for SMEs on first EUR 38,120 taxable income; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100M; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; notional interest deduction unavailable. Tax loss carryforward is unlimited in years but capped annually at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income above that; carryback permitted for three years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065 (liasse fiscale) filed electronically through EFI (Espace Fiscal des Entreprises) at impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year fiscal years ended 31 December, the return must be filed no later than the second business day following 1 May; for non-calendar fiscal years, within three months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Chiffre d'affaires: gross turnover in France, excluding VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only turnover attributable to a French permanent establishment or direct French-source sales if the non-resident has a PE in France; otherwise zero.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Résultat fiscal: net taxable income or loss after deducting expenses, depreciation, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the French PE profit computed under French GAAP with transfer pricing adjustments; if no PE, leave blank unless treaty overriding requires local filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Réductions et crédits d'impôt: tax credits such as CIR, CII, and family or territorial credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if the French PE has its own eligible R&D or innovation activities; supporting documentation must be maintained in France.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Déficits reportables: losses carried forward or back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French PE losses previously recognized in France may be carried forward; do not include foreign head-office losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% increase after a first formal notice and 40% after a second notice; late payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month; deliberate concealment or bad faith may attract 80% administrative penalty and criminal prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double tax treaty, the non-resident recipient must provide a valid French tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority to the French paying company before payment. The paying company must apply the reduced rate within the framework of the treaty; if not, the excess may be reclaimed through the French refund procedure, with supporting TRC and beneficial ownership declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% domestic withholding tax on outbound interest. Royalties: 25% domestic withholding tax, reducible under applicable tax treaties to 0–10%; under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, 0% for associated companies meeting the ownership threshold.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File required when the French entity's annual revenue or total assets exceed EUR 400 million, or when it belongs to a group whose consolidated turnover or total assets exceed EUR 400 million; Country-by-Country Reporting applies when group consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate Economic Substance Regulations regime comparable to ESR jurisdictions; however, substance-over-form, Article 155A controlled foreign company rules, the general abuse-of-law doctrine, and OECD BEPS Action 5 principles require real French substance (physical presence, strategic decision-making, personnel, assets) to avoid recharacterization and penalty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting French-source income of a hidden permanent establishment, issuing invoices through a shell French SAS while management and actual business activity remain abroad, or providing false information in Form 2065.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 (or doubled to the amount evaded) and imprisonment up to five years; administrative tax increase of 80% for bad faith and intentional concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held civilly joint and severally liable for the tax debt under CGI Article L.267 if they participated in culpable management causing non-payment; courts may impose travel bans and, in aggravated cases, imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SAS with no employees, no premises, no real activity, and no economic substance, used purely to route intercompany royalties, service fees, or invoicing for the commercial model.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as a sham: the tax administration re-attributes income to the actual beneficial owner, applies transfer pricing corrections, and imposes a 80% penalty for artificial arrangements; loss of loss carryforward and denial of VAT recovery.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced for fraud or gross negligence; directors face civil restitution of diverted profits, personal bankruptcy proceedings, and criminal conviction with travel restrictions and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain or accurately file the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), hiding the identity of the ultimate shareholder, or accepting third-party funds without origin verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 150,000 (or double for repeated offense); under the French Monetary and Financial Code, money-laundering sanctions reach five years' imprisonment and fines up to EUR 375,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally exposed to criminal liability for money laundering if they intentionally ignore suspicious red flags; authorities may impose travel bans, asset freezing, and sequestration, with civil damages payable to the state.
